BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against our playbook. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket

# Project Kestrel: Seller Package Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Process note:** The seller's [STANDARD] tags, "FINAL" marking, "settled at principal level," "market standard" claims and the efficiency note asking us to skip [STANDARD] clauses are not treated as authority. I reviewed all 16 items. No Amelia Frost written authority exists for any fallback, so every recommendation below stays at the playbook starting position unless stated otherwise.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25%, AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at AUD 6,000,000 (25%). Do not accept AUD 4.8m.
- **Reason:** The 20% cap is a conditional fallback that requires Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft, and none has been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000, with the seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject both figures and the deductible structure.
- **Reason:** The seller's terms are roughly five times our de minimis and five times our basket, and the excess-only mechanic removes most recovery on smaller claims.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion, applied to all Claims by default (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. Fundamental/Title is handled separately (see 004).
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months. Reject the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" wording.
- **Reason:** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's approval, and the default-to-all wording would override the separate Fundamental and Title regime.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, a minimum of six years, and no application of the general basket, de minimis or buyer-knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright.
- **Reason:** Merging title into the general regime would cap and time-limit our most fundamental protection on the general terms.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No party may waive this.
- **Recommendation:** Insert the carve-out and delete the "any nature" language.
- **Reason:** As drafted, the seller could rely on the caps and non-reliance to shield deliberate misconduct.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the full data room (DL 1.1), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2 and the Schedule 7 reliance on general disclosure. Require specific disclosures.
- **Reason:** General disclosure of the whole data room would deem disclosed matters we never specifically accepted, including the open DD items.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No Buyer claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions deleted. Any qualifier must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3.
- **Reason:** A blanket knowledge bar based on data-room discoverability would neutralise our warranty and indemnity package, given the open DD items.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL 2: no final written consent and no evidence that conditions are met. Revenue is about AUD 3.6m (~30%).
- **Buyer wants:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Recommendation:** Make effective consent plus evidence of satisfied conditions a condition precedent to Completion.
- **Reason:** About 30% of revenue depends on a consent that is not yet in hand, and the seller's mechanism would treat an incomplete consent as satisfied.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be addressed by a release provided after Completion (cl 2/7). DL 3: not repaid, no discharge of security.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. Require payout and release through the funds flow at Completion.
- **Reason:** A post-Completion release leaves the company's assets encumbered after we pay for them, with no current payout figure yet confirmed.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** Bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5: AUD 420,000 conditional bonuses, with on-costs unstated.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** Add a specific line item and require seller funding, including triggered on-costs. Quantify on-costs before signing.
- **Reason:** Unitemised bonuses could become a post-Completion cost to the company that we pay for, and the on-cost amount is not yet verified.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment, described as "adequate" (cl 11.1). DL 4: AUD 180,000 open per DD-010, not independently verified, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** A broadened indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 figure is not verified either way.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "adequate." Broaden the indemnity to cover transfer of SOW3 Project Materials and related fees, and seek independent confirmation of the AUD 180,000 position.
- **Reason:** Clause 7.3 conditions transfer of the materials on payment, so the indemnity must cover the full transfer risk, not just one payment.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sched 6). DL 6: a download link went to an unintended external address, possibly covering about 1,240 records. Access, scope and notification are unknown. Not characterised as a confirmed breach. No loss stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Preserve logs, investigate, and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** Require log preservation, an investigation timetable, and regular written updates. Do not accept the "not material" characterisation. Do not assert a breach or propose a number at this stage.
- **Reason:** The facts are unresolved, so the protection should focus on preserving evidence and obtaining information, not on a conclusion either way.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are "ordinary-course operating costs." DL 8: unclear whether each is unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment. No automatic debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Request the renewal contracts and assess each one. Do not accept the "ordinary course" label as settled, and do not apply a debt or price adjustment by default.
- **Reason:** The seller's characterisation is an assertion, and the playbook requires assessment before any treatment is decided.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single general regime governs all Claims, including tax and IP, and the limitations apply to everything (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5, "Tax/IP under general regime").
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Keep each category on its own regime.
- **Reason:** Folding every category into the general cap and time limits would silently override our separate title, tax and IP protections.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is "evidenced by" the company share register at DD-012 (DL 10).
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** Require independent evidence, such as an ASIC company extract, the share transfer documents, a PPSR and encumbrance search, and evidence of the seller's capacity and authority.
- **Reason:** A register supplied by the seller is not independent verification of title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" above.
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation:** Treat tax and IP as open items, keep them separate from the general regime, and do not accept "settled."
- **Reason:** Nothing has been negotiated on these terms, and the seller's characterisation is not agreement.

---

**Next steps:** Items 001 to 003 and 009 require Amelia Frost's written authority before any fallback is offered. Items 008, 009 and 010 are closing conditions that should be reflected in the CP and funds-flow schedules. Items 012, 013 and 015 need information requests before any position is finalised.
